reason: The wheels need powered drives, so the matched gearmotors look like a natural fit.

alternatives.reason: Preparing the remote also looks useful, but the rover needs drives first.

effect: The wheels and gearmotors are now wheel drives, ready for the deck; the gearboxes trade speed for turning force.
reaction: The explanation of the gearboxes makes the pairing more meaningful.
reason: The deck has a named Wheel drives slot, and the assembled drives should fit there.
expectation: The wheel drives will fit into the rover deck.

effect: The wheel drives are installed, and the remaining deck fittings can be added in any order.
reaction: The explanation of steering by different wheel speeds is interesting.

expectation: The ball caster will fit into the deck.

effect: The caster is installed alongside the wheel drives; the electrical modules remain to be fitted.
reaction: The straightforward fit is useful progress.

reaction: The fittings are straightforward so far.

reaction: That was a predictable preparation step.
reason: The gear guards appear intended to cover the rover's wheel drives before testing.
expectation: The guards will fit over the rover's drive mechanisms.

effect: The rover is wired and guarded, with its wheels safely raised for a remote test.
reaction: The test stops make the first powered test feel purposeful.
reason: The result says the guarded rover is ready for the remote.
expectation: The remote will operate the raised wheels so their responses can be tested.

effect: The remote test confirmed that the two wheel drives respond independently, completing the chapter’s goal.
reaction: Seeing the different wheel responses made the earlier steering explanation concrete.

mostWorthwhile.text: Testing the raised wheels was the most worthwhile part: it connected the assembled parts to the idea of steering with different wheel speeds.

leastWorthwhile.text: The successive electrical module fittings were straightforward but repetitive; they offered few meaningful decisions.

surprise.text: I found it interesting that the rover can turn by driving its wheels at different speeds, without a steering axle.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary: the parts had clear places or purposes, even when fitting them was predictable.

continue.text: I would choose to continue to see how the rover earns its pen and draws, though I hope the next chapter offers more decisions than the repeated fittings here.
